bifurcation.reason: This piece changes five strings of dialogue and one data-fold function. No visual reference is cited anywhere in this verdict, and no fidelity/art-direction claim is made. The one place a visual judgement WOULD be required — whether the 24 restored books paginate and turn correctly on screen — is declared unmeasured, not scored.

what_i_could_not_do: NO BROWSER, BY INSTRUCTION. The box is over its HAZARDS §29 contention ceiling and the brief directed me to prove consumption in Node as the builder did. I therefore did NOT run `node tools/contention.mjs` and did NOT open a browser. Consequence, stated plainly: I never saw a single pixel of either fix. The new greeting was never read on screen, its line-wrap in the dialogue window was never checked, and none of the 24 restored books was ever opened, paginated or page-turned. CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.2b's requirement to drive an interface with the real input path is UNMET for the reading screen, and I score its arms fail-closed rather than assuming they are fine.

I COULD NOT DEMONSTRATE THAT THE RUNNING ENGINE CONSUMES `foldBooks()`. I verified `Engine._buildUI()` calls it by READING game/src/engine.js:4577 — which CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.1 permits for locating and diagnosing, and forbids as the basis of a score. Every coupling number I report is measured at the function level (`foldBooks`, `wrap`, `greetingFor` called directly on real shipped data), not through a booted Engine. Control C proves this distinction has teeth: with engine.js reverted to its old inline fold, all three of the piece's checks still exit 0.

BLIND GATES NOT RUN — `not_possible`, failed closed. Both governing items carry `blind_pair: yes` (RI-DLG03 step 8, RI-UIX05 K10). A blind gate needs a fresh judge with no project context; I am a subagent, I cannot spawn subagents, and `create_session` is approval-gated so rule 0 forbids it. This is the structural hole CLAUDE.md §0e names, and it sits with the orchestrator, not with this piece. Honest census, derived this turn: `grep -rl "blind_pair: yes" corpus/ --include=*.md | grep -E '/RI-[^/]*\.md$' | wc -l` returns **82** (the brief said 81; the difference is one item added since, and my number is the one I derived).

I DID NOT RUN `tools/harness/w1-library-skillbooks.mjs`. It is browser-based, and the builder flagged the same omission. `foldBooks()` changes WHICH record wins a collision and never any field of the winning record, so skill-book grants should be unaffected — but 'should be' is not a measurement and I did not take one.

I DID NOT AUDIT THE BOOK-CONTENT SIDE. Whether the 14,670 restored words are GOOD (RI-LOR03 owns book content) is untouched here. I proved the words arrive at the wrapper; I did not read them for quality beyond the five samples quoted.

MY OWN SWEEP IS SCOPED BY WHAT I COULD TRACE. I collected 4,284 rendered strings by tracing consumers in converse.js, refusal.js and text.js this turn. If a rendered surface exists that I did not trace, my sweep is blind to it exactly as the builder's check is blind to faction-refusals. I name the surfaces I traced in the artifacts so the next critic can falsify the list rather than inherit it.

headline: BOTH FIXES ARE REAL AND EVERY NUMBER THE BUILDER CLAIMED SURVIVED INDEPENDENT RE-DERIVATION — including the two it corrected against the brief. The piece fails on its GUARDS, not its fixes: the standing check for defect 1 provably cannot fail on the file the defect lived in, because it regenerates that file before scanning it, and it is blind to 59 spoken lines; and no check notices if the engine stops calling the fixed fold at all.

biggest_gap.what: `tools/dialogue/check-authoring-leaks.mjs` does not measure what it says it measures, in two independent ways, both demonstrated. (1) IT ERASES THE DEFECT AND THEN REPORTS ITS ABSENCE. Importing `gen-greetings.mjs` has a top-level write side-effect, so the check REGENERATES `game/data/dialogue/greetings.json` before scanning it. Control D: a leak hand-authored into the shipped file is present before the run (grep = 1), gone after it (grep = 0), and the check exits 0 reporting PASS. That file holds 1,500 of the 4,988 strings the check reaches — 30.1% of its own shipped-data surface — and it is the file this very defect lived in. (2) IT IS BLIND TO SPOKEN LINES UNDER KEYS IT DOES NOT WHITELIST. `TEXT_KEYS` is a six-name allow-list; `faction-refusals.json` carries 59 player-facing strings across 7 factions under `reputation`, `attribute`, `skill_1`, `skill_2`, `world_state`, `welcome`, `rivalry_locked` and `not_joinable.*`, every one spoken by `FactionRefusals.speak()` (sim/quest/refusal.js) and reaching the player as a toast. Control E: `TODO: say it in one line. Placeholder — keep it short, writer.` injected into `factions.the_rootkeepers.reputation` -> check exits 0, PASS. The check's own header claims the opposite: 'a leak authored directly into a hand-written JSON file (not generated) is caught too.' Its `--self-test` cannot see either problem, because it only re-checks that the PATTERN list still matches a known string — it asserts nothing about whether the SCAN reaches anywhere.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This is the sixth check this project has found that could not fail, and it is the worst-shaped one yet: the previous five were blind, this one is actively destructive — it deletes the evidence and reports the absence of evidence, so a hand-authored leak in shipped dialogue is not merely missed but silently reverted, and the run looks green. Meanwhile the hand-written dialogue files that are being actively authored right now are exactly the ones outside its reach, so the next writer-instruction leak lands where the guard cannot see it and ships to the player's face in an NPC's mouth.
biggest_gap.remedy: Make the check read-only and scope it by renderedness rather than by key name, in `tools/dialogue/check-authoring-leaks.mjs`. Concretely: (a) stop importing `gen-greetings.mjs` for its side-effect — import `buildPools` from a module with no top-level write, or shell out to `node tools/dialogue/gen-greetings.mjs --check` and read its exit code, so the check never writes to `game/data/**`; add an assertion that the sha256 of `greetings.json` is unchanged across the run and exit non-zero if it moved. (b) Replace the `TEXT_KEYS` allow-list with an explicit RENDERED-SURFACE manifest derived from the consumers — at minimum `greetings.json` `pools[].lines[]`, `greetings/**` `greetings[].x`, `topics/**` `topics[].infos[].x` and `topics[].name`, `rumours.json` `.x`, `road-directions.json` `.text`, `faction-refusals.json` `factions.*.{reputation,attribute,skill_1,skill_2,world_state,welcome,rivalry_locked}` + `not_joinable.*` + `unknown_faction`, and `books/**` `books[].{text,title,author}` — and fail the check if it collects fewer than 4,200 strings, so a future refactor that silently narrows the surface goes red instead of quiet. (c) Extend `--self-test` with the two arms that would have caught this: inject the known leak into a hand-written file under a non-whitelisted spoken key and assert exit 1, and inject it into `greetings.json` on disk and assert exit 1. DONE = `bash corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-DIALOGUE-AUTHORING-LEAK-critic/scripts/controls.sh` prints EXIT=1 for CONTROL D and CONTROL E.

secondary_observations: NOT WORK FOR THE NEXT BUILDER, and a close second for biggest gap: no check notices if the engine stops calling the fix. CONTROL C reverts `game/src/engine.js:4577` to the old inline fold, leaving `foldBooks()` perfectly correct — the running game ships 24 undefined books again — and check-book-fold, check-authoring-leaks and check-greeting-consumer all exit 0. `check-book-fold.mjs`'s header asserts 'a pass here is a pass for the real consumer, not a parallel simulation that could drift from it'; that is RI-MTH07 §D3's 'a comment asserting a check is not a check', verbatim. The cheap fix is one arm: assert `game/src/engine.js` contains no second book fold and that `_buildUI` references `foldBooks`; the honest fix is to boot the engine once in the check.

The replacement greeting is a correct fix and mediocre writing. `The writ says nothing about talk.` is in-world, in register, and not filler — the brief's guard holds and the band still has five stances. But it does not earn its faction: of the 30 lines in greetings.json containing 'writ', 25 are RG-LEDGER's and 5 are this one, and it transplants natively into RG-LEDGER, RG-COURT and RG-EMPIRE while three of RG-BWC's other four cold lines name a Company-proper referent. The builder's own precedent shows what was lost — the camp greeting is 'OUR writ is out of Leyawiin', possessive and located. CLAUDE.md: Morrowind wins everywhere outside the fight, and a greeting is how a town tells you what it is.

`check-greeting-consumer.mjs`'s perturbation arm is dead as shipped. It reads the pre-fix source via `git show HEAD:tools/dialogue/gen-greetings.mjs`; now that the fix is committed, HEAD carries it, and the arm prints '(perturbation skipped)' and exits 0 forever. The builder's status file reports that arm's result as evidence, which was true when run pre-commit and is not reproducible now. The check DOES still fail on a real regression (Control B, exit 1), so this is a lost control rather than a vacuous check. Pin the pre-fix blob SHA instead of HEAD.

The builder found and reported honestly, and I verified, three things it did not have to: `the-drowned-ford` is genuinely uncatalogued in manifest.json (it is the 163rd id, a single-book doc with 384 chars caught by the fold's other branch); the three other `Object.values(this.data.books)` folds at engine.js:2887, :2946 and :5522 are all safe, the last one by accident because 0 of manifest's 162 stubs carry a `knowledge_key`; and the broader 43-hit sweep was not wired into the standing check. All three claims are exactly true. This is the reporting standard the project asks for.

The fix is stronger than the builder claimed. Across 500 shuffled load orders the old fold's textless-book count ranges 0..162 — pre-fix, the blast radius was a pure accident of `index.json` ordering and could have been the entire catalogue. The real `foldBooks()` was byte-identical to baseline in 500 of 500.

A second live NPC was affected and unnamed: `blackwood-company-camp` (disposition 20) sits in the same RG-BWC cold cell as `blackwood-company-factor` (25). Both spoke the leak pre-fix; both are fixed. The builder's consumption proof used only one.

corpus_extended.finding: The lint regex is quoted in the item as `\b(quest|objective|marker|...)` — unanchored at the right-hand end, so `\bquest` matches the word `question`. Run verbatim over the shipped greeting and rumour corpus it returns 46 hits against a threshold of 0, on a dimension the item marks as an AUTOMATIC FAIL filed as AR-2 leakage. 45 of the 46 are the word 'question'. As written, the item's own instrument fails the build for containing ordinary English.
corpus_extended.proposed_correction: Right-anchor the alternation: `\b(quests?|objectives?|markers?|waypoints?|your (map|journal|compass)|coordinates?|[0-9] ?(m|metres|meters|yards)|head (north|south|east|west) [0-9])\b`. On the current corpus this returns 5 rather than 46.
corpus_extended.not_built_here: I did not edit RI-DLG03. CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3 permits a critic to ADD to the bar and forbids weakening it, and anchoring a regex NARROWS what fails — which is a relaxation, however obviously correct, and therefore not mine to make unilaterally. It goes to the item's owner or to arbitration.

corpus_extended.finding: No reference item in the corpus governs authoring-instruction leakage into shipped text. I checked: `grep -rli 'authoring instruction|writer.s instruction|placeholder text|meta-instruction' corpus/ --include=*.md` returns ZERO files. RI-DLG03's step-7 lint is the nearest thing and its pattern set is entirely about Souls UI vocabulary (quest/objective/marker/waypoint/coordinates) — it has no pattern for a brief to a writer, and would not have caught 'Say it in one line.' The defect this piece fixed was found by a BLIND JUDGE looking at a screenshot, not by any bar we own.
corpus_extended.proposed_correction: A short reference item — provisionally RI-DLG10, 'text hygiene: the writer must not be audible' — setting a rendered-surface manifest, a pattern class for meta-authoring language, and the two negative-control arms named in the biggest gap's remedy. It should judge the SURFACE (does the scan reach every string the player can read) and not only the PATTERNS, because that is the axis both this piece's check and my own sweep are weakest on.
corpus_extended.not_built_here: CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3 guard 3 — bounded. Writing the item properly means enumerating every rendered surface in the game, which is a piece of work, not a pass. I have filed the finding and named what is needed, and I state the cap this puts on my own verdict: the sweep I ran is scoped to the surfaces I could trace in one session, and a leak on a surface I did not find is invisible to me exactly as it is to the builder's check.

self_audit.judged_output_not_source_note: Every score rests on a script's output over real shipped data. Source was read only for locating, quoting authored text, and diagnosing — enumerated in source_reads.
